title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of visuospatial attentional deficits in Parkinson's patients
title_zh: 帕金森病患者视觉空间注意缺陷的系统综述与荟萃分析
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition primarily characterized by motor deficits, yet cognitive impairments are increasingly recognized. While deficits in executive functioning are well documented even in the absence of cognitive decline, evidence of attentional deficits in PD remains inconsistent, and the role of motor symptom lateralization is unclear. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we examined visual attention in right-handed, cognitively unimpaired idiopathic PD patients, focusing on the canonical attentional domains (sustained, selective, divided) and processes (alerting, endogenous and exogenous orienting, reorienting), as well as visuospatial bias. Four databases were searched for studies comparing PD patients with healthy controls. Meta-analytic estimates were derived using Hedges' g within random-effects models, and studies that could not be quantitatively integrated were summarized narratively. In addition, studies directly comparing patients with left- and right-predominant motor symptoms (LPD vs. RPD) were reviewed qualitatively. Across 51 studies, PD patients exhibited deficits in sustained, selective, and divided attention. Among attentional processes, only exogenous orienting was impaired, whereas alerting, endogenous orienting, and reorienting were preserved. Findings from the few studies examining visuospatial bias indicated small, context-dependent shifts in spatial attention rather than a consistent directional bias. These findings indicate that PD patients show visual-attentional impairments, particularly under high-demand conditions, while basic alertness and voluntary orienting appear preserved. Exogenous orienting deficits and subtle rightward spatial tendencies in LPD suggest disruption of right-hemisphere attentional networks. These results have implications for early cognitive assessment, rehabilitation strategies, and understanding the neural bases of attentional dysfunction in PD.
abstract_zh: 帕金森病（PD）主要表现为运动障碍，但其认知损害日益受到重视。即使患者尚无认知衰退，执行功能缺陷也已有充分证据，注意缺陷的研究结论及运动症状侧化的作用仍不一致。本系统综述与荟萃分析考察右利手、认知未受损的特发性 PD 患者的视觉注意，涵盖持续性、选择性和分配性注意，以及警觉、内源性与外源性定向、再定向和视觉空间偏倚。研究检索了四个数据库，采用随机效应模型和 Hedges' g 汇总可量化结果，并对其余研究及左侧与右侧运动症状占优势患者的直接比较进行叙述性分析。51 项研究显示，PD 患者的持续性、选择性和分配性注意均受损；在具体注意过程中，仅外源性定向受损，警觉、内源性定向和再定向相对保留。少量视觉空间偏倚研究仅发现幅度较小、依赖情境的空间注意偏移，未形成一致的方向性偏倚。结果表明，PD 患者在高负荷条件下尤其容易出现视觉注意障碍，但基本警觉和自主定向仍较完整。左侧症状占优势患者的外源性定向缺陷及轻微右偏趋势提示右半球注意网络可能受扰。这些发现有助于早期认知评估、康复策略制定及理解 PD 注意功能障碍的神经基础。
